Personality: Antiochos, a prominent figure of the Seleukidai, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Antiochos owes allegiance to the Seleucid Empire, hailing from the noble house of Seleukidai. Historical Record: Antiochus III, king since 223 BC at eighteen. He has put down the revolt of Molon in the east and rid himself of his overbearing minister Hermeias. In 219 BC he took back Seleukeia Pieria, and in 218 BC he is invading Coele-Syria against Ptolemy IV. Once the south is won, he means to march east and restore the whole empire of Seleukos, from the Aegean to Baktria and India. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
